[E_DIV_REAL_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Div** divides tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the quotient of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \frac{\tilde{A}[i]}{\tilde{B}[i]} $$ where - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - the quotient is the quotient in $\mathbb{R}$ of the two elements. The division is exact: $C[i]$ is the quotient in $\mathbb{R}$, with no approximation. **Domain.** The quotient of two real numbers exists only when the divisor is non-null. The domain of the operator is therefore the set of pairs of real tensors whose divisor has no null element, i.e. $\forall i,\ \tilde{B}[i] \neq 0$; that condition is the precondition stated by constraint [E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_B_0010](#E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_B_0010) on tensor $B$. For every pair of tensors that satisfies it, the result is the one given above. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the quotient of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. No quotient is formed for an empty result, so that the domain condition bears on the elements of $\tilde{B}$ only. [END]
- `[E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_A_0010]` Shape compatibility - Statement: The shapes of $A$ and $B$ are compatible for broadcasting.

- `[E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_B_0010]` Non-null divisor - Statement: Every element of $\tilde{B}$, the divisor broadcast to the shape of $C$, is non-null, i.e. $\forall i,\ \tilde{B}[i] \neq 0$. - Rationale: The quotient of two real numbers exists only when the divisor is non-null; the condition is the domain of the operator, stated in [E_DIV_REAL_FUNC_0010](#E_DIV_REAL_FUNC_0010).
- `[E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_B_0020]` Shape compatibility - Statement: see constraint [E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_A_0010](#E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_A_0010) on tensor $A$.

- `[E_DIV_REAL_CONSTR_C_0010]` Shape definition
  - Statement: Tensor $C$ has the shape of $A$ and $B$ broadcast to a common shape.

[E_DIV_FLOAT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Div** divides tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise according to IEEE 754 floating-point semantics and stores the result in tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the floating-point quotient of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below. No element of $B$ is excluded: every combination of operands of the type, including the special numbers, has a result of the type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \tilde{A}[i] /_{(\text{f})} \tilde{B}[i] = \begin{cases} \text{NaN} & \text{if } \tilde{A}[i] \text{ or } \tilde{B}[i] \text{ is NaN} \\ \text{NaN} & \text{if } \tilde{A}[i] \text{ and } \tilde{B}[i] \text{ are both } \pm\infty, \text{ or both } \pm 0 \\ \pm\infty & \text{if } \tilde{A}[i] \text{ is finite and non-null and } \tilde{B}[i] \text{ is } \pm 0, \text{ or } \tilde{A}[i] \text{ is } \pm\infty \text{ and } \tilde{B}[i] \text{ is finite and non-null} \\ \pm 0 & \text{if } \tilde{A}[i] \text{ is } \pm 0 \text{ and } \tilde{B}[i] \text{ is finite and non-null, or } \tilde{A}[i] \text{ is finite and } \tilde{B}[i] \text{ is } \pm\infty \\ \text{round}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} $$ where - $/_{(\text{f})}$ is the division of the floating-point type of $A$, $B$ and $C$, i.e. $/_{(\text{f16})}$, $/_{(\text{f32})}$ or $/_{(\text{f64})}$ according to that type, whereas the $/$ of the last case is the division of $\mathbb{R}$: there, $\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact quotient of the two elements, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $\pm$ in the third and fourth cases is the sign of the exact quotient: $+$ when the two operands have the same sign and $-$ when they have opposite signs, - $\text{round}(x)$ is the value of $x$ rounded to the nearest value of the type of $A$ and $B$ using the roundTiesToEven attribute of IEEE 754, the exponent range of the type being unbounded when deciding an overflow: a magnitude whose rounded value exceeds the largest finite value of the type gives an infinity of the sign of $x$, and a magnitude below the smallest subnormal value of the type gives a zero of the sign of $x$. **Operands that are NaN.** The first case propagates the NaN: a NaN operand gives a NaN result, whatever the other operand is. The NaN of this case is a quiet NaN; its sign and its payload are not specified, so that every quiet NaN of the type of $A$ and $B$ is a conforming result. **Invalid operation.** The second case is the invalid operation of IEEE 754 section 7.2 for division: the quotient $\infty/\infty$ and the quotient $0/0$ have no value in the extended reals, and the result is NaN, again any quiet NaN of the type. **Division by zero.** The third case is the division-by-zero exception of IEEE 754: a finite non-null dividend divided by a zero gives an infinity whose sign is the sign of the exact quotient, so that $1.0/(+0)$ gives $+\infty$ and $-1.0/(+0)$ gives $-\infty$. The division of an infinity by a finite non-null value also gives an infinity, of the sign of the exact quotient; that case is not an exception of the standard, the result being the limit of the quotients of the finite values. **Null quotients.** The fourth case gives a null result whose sign is the sign of the exact quotient: $\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]$ is null when the dividend is null and the divisor is finite non-null, and when the divisor is infinite and the dividend is finite. The signs of the operands then decide the sign of the zero: $(+0)/2.0$ gives $+0$ and $(-0)/2.0$ gives $-0$, while $(+0)/(-2.0)$ gives $-0$. A null dividend divided by a null divisor is not a null quotient: it falls in the second case and gives NaN. The last case also produces a null result when a non-null exact quotient is so small that it rounds to zero; its sign is then the sign of that exact quotient as well. **Finite operands.** In the last case both operands are finite and the divisor is non-null, so that the exact quotient is a non-null real number. The result is that quotient rounded as defined above. When the exact quotient is representable in the type, no rounding takes place; otherwise the result is the nearest value of the type, and it may be a subnormal value, a zero, or an infinity when the exponent of the exact quotient exceeds the largest exponent of the type. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the quotient of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]

[E_DIV_INT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Div** divides tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in output tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the quotient of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below, truncated toward zero. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same signed $n$-bit type, and the result is a value of that type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \begin{cases} \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) & \text{if } -2^{n-1} \le \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) \le 2^{n-1}-1 \\[4pt] \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) - 2^n & \text{if } \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) \notin [-2^{n-1},\, 2^{n-1}-1] \end{cases} $$ where - $\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact quotient of the two elements, the quotient in $\mathbb{Q}$ of two integers whose divisor is non-null, - $\operatorname{trunc}(x)$ is the integer part of $x$, i.e. $x$ rounded toward zero: $\operatorname{trunc}(x) = \lfloor x \rfloor$ when $x \ge 0$ and $\operatorname{trunc}(x) = \lceil x \rceil$ when $x < 0$, so that $\operatorname{trunc}(3.5) = 3$ and $\operatorname{trunc}(-3.5) = -3$, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $n$ is the number of bits of the type of $A$ and $B$. The second case is the complement of the first: exactly one of the two cases applies to every pair of operands whose divisor is non-null, and the result is then determined. **Truncating division.** The quotient $\operatorname{trunc}(a/b)$ is the unique integer $q$ such that $a = q \cdot b + r$, with $|r| < |b|$ and with $r$ null or of the sign of $a$. It is the quotient ONNX prescribes for the integer types, and it differs from the floor: for `int8`, $7/2 = 3$ and $-7/2 = -3$, whereas the floor of $-3.5$ is $-4$. The sign of the result is the sign of the exact quotient: the quotient of two operands of the same sign is non-negative, and the quotient of two operands of opposite signs is non-positive, so that a null result is the neutral value $0$ of the type, with no sign. **The one quotient outside the range.** The values of an $n$-bit signed type lie in $[-2^{n-1}, 2^{n-1}-1]$, so that the quotient of two of its values, truncated toward zero, lies in $[-2^{n-1}, 2^{n-1}]$: the lower bound is reached by $(-2^{n-1})/1 = -2^{n-1}$, and the upper bound only by $(-2^{n-1})/(-1) = 2^{n-1}$. Only the value $2^{n-1}$ leaves the range of the type, so that the second case of the definition is the case $\operatorname{trunc}(\tilde{A}[i]/\tilde{B}[i]) = 2^{n-1}$, reached by that single pair of operands; the result is then $2^{n-1} - 2^n = -2^{n-1}$. For `int8`, $-128 / -1$ gives $-128$; the exact quotient $128$ is represented by the value of the type that is congruent to it modulo $2^8$. **A null divisor.** No element of $B$ is excluded, so that a null element of $B$ makes the exact quotient undefined and the result of the operator undetermined; the condition is described in the "Error conditions" section. Every other pair of operands falls in one of the two cases above, and the result is fully determined. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the quotient of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. No quotient is formed for an empty result, so that a null element of $B$ in an empty tensor raises no condition. [END]

[E_DIV_UINT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Div** divides tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in output tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the quotient of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below, truncated toward zero. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same unsigned $n$-bit type, and the result is a value of that type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \left\lfloor \frac{\tilde{A}[i]}{\tilde{B}[i]} \right\rfloor $$ where - $\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact quotient of the two elements, the quotient in $\mathbb{Q}$ of two integers whose divisor is non-null, - $\lfloor \cdot \rfloor$ is the floor, which for two non-negative operands is the quotient truncated toward zero, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$. **The result never leaves the range of the type.** The operands are non-negative, so that their exact quotient is non-negative and its floor is at most the dividend: $0 \le \lfloor a/b \rfloor \le a \le 2^n-1$ for every $b \ge 1$. The result of a division by a non-null element is therefore the floor itself, with no reduction modulo $2^n$ and no overflow, and it is exact in the type. For `uint8`, $200/3$ gives $66$ and $255/255$ gives $1$. The truncation and the floor coincide on the unsigned types, so that the distinction between them, which the signed types make visible, has no effect here. **A null divisor.** No element of $B$ is excluded, so that a null element of $B$ makes the exact quotient undefined and the result of the operator undetermined; the condition is described in the "Error conditions" section, and it is the only condition under which the result is not the value given above. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the quotient of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. No quotient is formed for an empty result, so that a null element of $B$ in an empty tensor raises no condition. [END]

  - Statement: Tensor $C$ has the shape of $A$ and $B$ broadcast to a common shape.

examples.excerpt:
### Example 1

For the `int8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & -7 & 7 & -7 & -128 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2 & -2 & -2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -3 & -3 & 3 & -128 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The first four quotients are $3.5$, $-3.5$, $-3.5$ and $3.5$: each is truncated toward zero, which gives $3$, $-3$, $-3$ and $3$, and not the floors $-3.5 \to -4$. The last quotient is $(-128)/(-1) = 128$, which exceeds the maximum value $127$ of `int8`: the second case of the definition applies and the result is $128 - 2^8 = -128$, the value of the type congruent to $128$ modulo $2^8$.

### Example 1

For the `uint8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 200 & 255 & 6 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 255 & 6 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 66 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The quotient $7/2 = 3.5$ is truncated toward zero and gives $3$; $200/3 = 66.67$ gives $66$; $255/255 = 1$ and $6/6 = 1$ are exact. Each of the four results lies in the range $[0, 255]$ of `uint8`, as every quotient of the type does.

The NaN of this case is a quiet NaN; its sign and its payload are not specified, so that every quiet NaN of the type of $A$ and $B$ is a conforming result. **Invalid operation.** The second case is the invalid operation of IEEE 754 section 7.2 for division: the quotient $\infty/\infty$ and the quotient $0/0$ have no value in the extended reals, and the result is NaN, again any quiet NaN of the type. **Division by zero.** The third case is the division-by-zero exception of IEEE 754: a finite non-null dividend divided by a zero gives an infinity whose sign is the sign of the exact quotient, so that $1.0/(+0)$ gives $+\infty$ and $-1.0/(+0)$ gives $-\infty$. The division of an infinity by a finite non-null value also gives an infinity, of the sign of the exact quotient; that case is not an exception of the standard, the result being the limit of the quotients of the finite values. **Null quotients.** The fourth case gives a null result whose sign is the sign of the exact quotient: $\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]$ is null when the dividend is null and the divisor is finite non-null, and when the divisor is infinite and the dividend is finite. The signs of the operands then decide the sign of the zero: $(+0)/2.0$ gives $+0$ and $(-0)/2.0$ gives $-0$, while $(+0)/(-2.0)$ gives $-0$. A null dividend divided by a null divisor is not a null quotient: it falls in the second case and gives NaN. The last case also produces a null result when a non-null exact quotient is so small that it rounds to zero; its sign is then the sign of that exact quotient as well. **Finite operands.** In the last case both operands are finite and the divisor is non-null, so that the exact quotient is a non-null real number. The result is that quotient rounded as defined above. When the exact quotient is representable in the type, no rounding takes place; otherwise the result is the nearest value of the type, and it may be a subnormal value, a zero, or an infinity when the exponent of the exact quotient exceeds the largest exponent of the type. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the quotient of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]

[E_DIV_INT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Div** divides tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in output tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the quotient of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below, truncated toward zero. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same signed $n$-bit type, and the result is a value of that type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \begin{cases} \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) & \text{if } -2^{n-1} \le \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) \le 2^{n-1}-1 \\[4pt] \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) - 2^n & \text{if } \operatorname{trunc}\!\left(\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]\right) \notin [-2^{n-1},\, 2^{n-1}-1] \end{cases} $$ where - $\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact quotient of the two elements, the quotient in $\mathbb{Q}$ of two integers whose divisor is non-null, - $\operatorname{trunc}(x)$ is the integer part of $x$, i.e. $x$ rounded toward zero: $\operatorname{trunc}(x) = \lfloor x \rfloor$ when $x \ge 0$ and $\operatorname{trunc}(x) = \lceil x \rceil$ when $x < 0$, so that $\operatorname{trunc}(3.5) = 3$ and $\operatorname{trunc}(-3.5) = -3$, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $n$ is the number of bits of the type of $A$ and $B$. The second case is the complement of the first: exactly one of the two cases applies to every pair of operands whose divisor is non-null, and the result is then determined. **Truncating division.** The quotient $\operatorname{trunc}(a/b)$ is the unique integer $q$ such that $a = q \cdot b + r$, with $|r| < |b|$ and with $r$ null or of the sign of $a$. It is the quotient ONNX prescribes for the integer types, and it differs from the floor: for `int8`, $7/2 = 3$ and $-7/2 = -3$, whereas the floor of $-3.5$ is $-4$. The sign of the result is the sign of the exact quotient: the quotient of two operands of the same sign is non-negative, and the quotient of two operands of opposite signs is non-positive, so that a null result is the neutral value $0$ of the type, with no sign. **The one quotient outside the range.** The values of an $n$-bit signed type lie in $[-2^{n-1}, 2^{n-1}-1]$, so that the quotient of two of its values, truncated toward zero, lies in $[-2^{n-1}, 2^{n-1}]$: the lower bound is reached by $(-2^{n-1})/1 = -2^{n-1}$, and the upper bound only by $(-2^{n-1})/(-1) = 2^{n-1}$. Only the value $2^{n-1}$ leaves the range of the type, so that the second case of the definition is the case $\operatorname{trunc}(\tilde{A}[i]/\tilde{B}[i]) = 2^{n-1}$, reached by that single pair of operands; the result is then $2^{n-1} - 2^n = -2^{n-1}$. For `int8`, $-128 / -1$ gives $-128$; the exact quotient $128$ is represented by the value of the type that is congruent to it modulo $2^8$. **A null divisor.** No element of $B$ is excluded, so that a null element of $B$ makes the exact quotient undefined and the result of the operator undetermined; the condition is described in the "Error conditions" section. Every other pair of operands falls in one of the two cases above, and the result is fully determined. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the quotient of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. No quotient is formed for an empty result, so that a null element of $B$ in an empty tensor raises no condition. [END]

[E_DIV_UINT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Div** divides tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in output tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the quotient of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below, truncated toward zero. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same unsigned $n$-bit type, and the result is a value of that type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \left\lfloor \frac{\tilde{A}[i]}{\tilde{B}[i]} \right\rfloor $$ where - $\tilde{A}[i] / \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact quotient of the two elements, the quotient in $\mathbb{Q}$ of two integers whose divisor is non-null, - $\lfloor \cdot \rfloor$ is the floor, which for two non-negative operands is the quotient truncated toward zero, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$. **The result never leaves the range of the type.** The operands are non-negative, so that their exact quotient is non-negative and its floor is at most the dividend: $0 \le \lfloor a/b \rfloor \le a \le 2^n-1$ for every $b \ge 1$. The result of a division by a non-null element is therefore the floor itself, with no reduction modulo $2^n$ and no overflow, and it is exact in the type. For `uint8`, $200/3$ gives $66$ and $255/255$ gives $1$. The truncation and the floor coincide on the unsigned types, so that the distinction between them, which the signed types make visible, has no effect here. **A null divisor.** No element of $B$ is excluded, so that a null element of $B$ makes the exact quotient undefined and the result of the operator undetermined; the condition is described in the "Error conditions" section, and it is the only condition under which the result is not the value given above. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the quotient of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. No quotient is formed for an empty result, so that a null element of $B$ in an empty tensor raises no condition. [END]

### Example 1

For the `int8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & -7 & 7 & -7 & -128 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2 & -2 & -2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -3 & -3 & 3 & -128 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The first four quotients are $3.5$, $-3.5$, $-3.5$ and $3.5$: each is truncated toward zero, which gives $3$, $-3$, $-3$ and $3$, and not the floors $-3.5 \to -4$. The last quotient is $(-128)/(-1) = 128$, which exceeds the maximum value $127$ of `int8`: the second case of the definition applies and the result is $128 - 2^8 = -128$, the value of the type congruent to $128$ modulo $2^8$.

### Example 1

For the `uint8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 200 & 255 & 6 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 255 & 6 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 66 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The quotient $7/2 = 3.5$ is truncated toward zero and gives $3$; $200/3 = 66.67$ gives $66$; $255/255 = 1$ and $6/6 = 1$ are exact. Each of the four results lies in the range $[0, 255]$ of `uint8`, as every quotient of the type does.
